ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that point $E$ is a point inside rectangle $ABCD$, satisfying $\angle AEB=90^\circ$. Extend $DE$ to intersect the semicircle with diameter $CD$ at point $F$. When $AE=20$, $BE=15$, and $DF=24$, what is the length of the side $AD$ of the rectangle?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the diagram, extend a line from point E to draw EH $\perp$ CD at H, intersecting AB at point T, and connect CF.\\
Since quadrilateral ABCD is a rectangle,\\
therefore AB=CD, AB$\parallel$CD,\\
since $\angle$AEB=90$^\circ$, AE=20, BE=15,\\
therefore AB=$\sqrt{AE^2+BE^2}=\sqrt{20^2+15^2}=25$,\\
since ET$\perp$AB,\\
therefore $\frac{1}{2}AE \cdot EB= \frac{1}{2}AB \cdot ET$,\\
therefore ET=$\frac{20\times 15}{25}=12$,\\
therefore AT=DH=$\sqrt{AE^2-ET^2}=\sqrt{20^2-12^2}=16$,\\
since CD is the diameter,\\
therefore $\angle$CFD=90$^\circ$,\\
therefore CF=$\sqrt{CD^2-DF^2}=\sqrt{25^2-24^2}=7$,\\
since $\angle$EDH=$\angle$CDF, $\angle$EHD=$\angle$CFD=90$^\circ$,\\
therefore $\triangle$DHE$\sim$$\triangle$DFC,\\
therefore $\frac{DH}{DF}=\frac{EH}{CF}$,\\
therefore $\frac{16}{24}=\frac{EH}{7}$,\\
therefore EH=$\frac{14}{3}$,\\
therefore AD=BC=HT=ET+EH=12+$\frac{14}{3}=\boxed{\frac{50}{3}}$.

ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: As shown in the figure, point $E$ lies inside rectangle $ABCD$ and satisfies $\angle AEB=90^\circ$. Extend $DE$ to intersect the semicircle with diameter $CD$ at point $F$. If $AE=20$, $BE=15$, and $DF=24$, find the length of side $AD$ of the rectangle.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Draw $EH \perp CD$ at $H$, with line $EH$ intersecting $AB$ at point $T$, and connect $CF$. Since $ABCD$ is a rectangle, $AB=CD$ and $AB\parallel CD$. Because $\angle AEB=90^\circ$, $AE=20$, and $BE=15$, we have $AB=\sqrt{AE^2+BE^2}=\sqrt{20^2+15^2}=25$. Since $ET\perp AB$, the area relation gives $\frac{1}{2}AE\cdot BE=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot ET$, so $ET=\frac{20\times 15}{25}=12$. Then $AT=DH=\sqrt{AE^2-ET^2}=\sqrt{20^2-12^2}=16$. Since $CD$ is the diameter, $\angle CFD=90^\circ$, so $CF=\sqrt{CD^2-DF^2}=\sqrt{25^2-24^2}=7$. Also, $\angle EDH=\angle CDF$ and $\angle EHD=\angle CFD=90^\circ$, so $\triangle DHE\sim\triangle DFC$. Therefore, $\frac{DH}{DF}=\frac{EH}{CF}$, hence $\frac{16}{24}=\frac{EH}{7}$, giving $EH=\frac{14}{3}$. Thus $AD=BC=HT=ET+EH=12+\frac{14}{3}=\frac{50}{3}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangle ABCD, A is at the upper left, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, D is at the upper right, and the right vertical side CD is the diameter of a semicircle curving toward the inside of the rectangle. Point E is located inside the rectangle; line segments AE and BE intersect at E and a right angle is marked; an oblique line starting from D passes through E and continues to point F on the semicircle, that is, D, E, F are collinear. According to the method, draw auxiliary lines: through E draw a horizontal line, intersecting the left vertical side AB at T and the right vertical side CD at H respectively, and connect CF. Reasoning: Because ∠AEB=90°, AE=20, BE=15, in right triangle AEB, AB is the hypotenuse, AB=sqrt(20^2+15^2)=25. Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so CD=AB=25. The perpendicular from E to AB is ET, namely the altitude drawn from the right-angle vertex E to the hypotenuse AB in right triangle AEB. By equality of areas, (1/2)AE·BE=(1/2)AB·ET, so ET=(20×15)/25=12. Thus AT=sqrt(AE^2-ET^2)=sqrt(20^2-12^2)=16. Since AB and CD are parallel and both are vertical sides, the horizontal line through E intersects AB and CD at T and H, so the vertical distances from the same horizontal height to the top side AD are equal, DH=AT=16. Because F is on the semicircle with CD as diameter, by the inscribed angle theorem, ∠CFD=90°. So in right triangle DCF, CF=sqrt(CD^2-DF^2)=sqrt(25^2-24^2)=7. Triangles DHE and DFC are both right triangles, and DE and DF are the same straight line, DH and DC are the same straight line, so they have one acute angle equal, therefore △DHE∼△DFC. Corresponding sides satisfy EH/CF=DH/DF, hence EH=CF·DH/DF=7×16/24=14/3. The horizontal width AD of the rectangle is equal to HT on the same horizontal line, and HT=ET+EH=12+14/3=50/3.
